comment: What the README says about a format beyond what the app itself knows. The names, suffixes, abilities and codecs come from src/renderer/src/utils/archivePaths.ts; this file holds only the prose and the detail no screen shows.

ZIP.notes: Expert mode picks the method: Deflate (8) by default, or Store (0), LZMA (14), Zstandard (93). Choosing Deflate or Zstandard brings that codec's own options with it. Password creation uses ZipCrypto by default; expert mode switches it to WinZip AES-256 or AES-128. Split sets use `.z01 … .zip`, with `.zip` as the representative file

7Z.notes: Reads solid archives and AES-encrypted data or headers. Password creation uses AES-256 and can optionally encrypt the header, which hides the file names. Split sets use `.7z.001 …`, with `.7z.001` as the representative file

TAR.notes: Stores multiple files without a compression codec

TAR.XZ.notes: Read-only. Reads every integrity check the container defines, streams cut into several blocks, and concatenated streams. A filter ahead of LZMA2 — BCJ or delta — is refused rather than misread

TAR.ZST.notes: Stores multiple files through TAR. Expert mode picks the search strategy, the window size, long distance matching, and the thread count

GZ.notes: Supports one file per stream. Expanded size and compression ratio remain unknown until extraction

ZST.notes: Supports one file per stream, with the same expert codec options as TAR.ZST. Expanded size and compression ratio remain unknown until extraction
